title: finding(react): usePageAssignment reads the refused alias `pageType` before `type`, so the first operand is unreachable — found by the census in a file this card's own text had already audited
body:
`packages/react/src/hooks/usePageAssignment.ts` reads `p.pageType` before falling back to `p.type`. **`PageSchema` refuses `pageType`** — and it names the canonical key itself: `pageType` is one of the schema's declared **aliases**, mapping to `type`.

⇒ the fallback is what decides, so **behaviour is right and the first operand is unreachable**.

## ⭐ Why this one is worth reading twice

This file is **one of the two files objectui#9438 already names**. A human had audited it by hand for that very card — and the census found a **third** read in it on its first run.

That is the whole argument for the instrument, demonstrated on the card's own evidence: a careful reading of a named file missed a live instance that a seam-anchored walk did not.

## Why it is class (b), despite behaving correctly today

The contract declares `pageType` an alias of `type` and refuses it as a key. Code that reads the alias first is reading a spelling the schema will never deliver:

- the operand is **dead** — unreachable by construction, not merely unused;
- it teaches the next reader that `pageType` is a live discriminator worth checking, which is exactly how the spelling propagates.

## ⚠️ A comment beside the read that the installed pin contradicts

The comment there says the designer-side spelling is *"still expressible in raw metadata"*. The installed spec pin (**17.4.0**) disagrees: a page carrying `pageType` is a **hard parse error**. ⇒ whoever takes this read should repair that sentence in the same stroke — it travels with the code it annotates, and this lane's governing line is 「门禁的自述必须为真」.

## ⛔ Why it was not repaired in PR #9670

Same reason as its sibling: objectui#9438 delivered the **walk**, and each live read is a renderer change with its own question. ⛔ Mixing an instrument with the judgements it surfaces is how an instrument stops being trusted.
